sentences.text: Mechanism cluster: Neurotransmitter release cycle (Reactome R-HSA-112310; membership stability S=1.00).
Pathway-anchored links within the SNARE/synaptic release axis: STXBP1, VAMP2, and SNAP25 co-participate in Acetylcholine (R-HSA-264642) and Serotonin (R-HSA-181429) Neurotransmitter Release Cycles.
GO annotations for STXBP1 emphasize vesicle trafficking: export from cell (GO:0002576) and vesicle organization (GO:0035493).
Additional synaptic pathways for STXBP1 include Transmission across Chemical Synapses (R-HSA-112315) and broader Neuronal System (R-HSA-112316).
Natural History Study in Pediatric Patients with STXBP1 Encephalopathy with Epilepsy (NCT05462054) serves STXBP1-related disease (DEE4).
STXBP1 and SYNGAP1 Related Disorders Natural History Study (NCT06555965) also serves STXBP1-related disease (DEE4).
The NCT05462054 asset is mapped cross-disease to STX1B-related disease (GEFS+, type 9) with reported phenotype coverage 55% (5/8; IC 16.98/30.76).
Community assets include Asociación Síndrome STXBP1 (Spain) and the European STXBP1 Consortium (ESCO).
A VAMP2-focused foundation (Raging Raymond Foundation) anchors within the same neurotransmitter release network.

sections.title: What differs and must be verified

sentences.text: Counterexample on mechanism: GNAO1-related disease (NEDIM) is phenotypically proximate yet mechanistically off-axis for neurotransmitter release and is excluded for current clustering purposes.
Variant-model differences: STXBP1 shows loss_of_function, whereas CACNA1A comparators include gain_of_function variants in epilepsy cohorts.
Variant-model differences: STXBP1 shows loss_of_function, whereas GRIN1 comparators include gain_of_function variants that increase NMDA receptor-mediated charge transfer.

Contradictory genotype–phenotype correlations within STXBP1 are reported: no correlation between seizure and ID severity; no correlation between mutation type and seizure/cognitive outcome; and no recurrent variant–syndrome specificity.
Rikke S Møller is a bridge across STX1B and STXBP1 work: authored STX1B disease papers and an STXBP1 natural history study relevant to data capture.
Ingo Helbig is active in STXBP1 community-building and phenotyping relevant to cross-disease capture.

Review NCT05462054 phenotype mapping coverage for STX1B-related disease (GEFS+, type 9) claimed as 0.55 (5/8; IC 16.98/30.76), and verify Rikke S Møller as contact based on authorship links to STX1B and the STXBP1 natural history asset.
Coverage of STX1B-related disease (GEFS+, type 9) phenotype information is reported as 55% (5/8; IC 16.98/30.76) using NCT05462054 mapping.

## What differs and must be verified
Counterexample on mechanism: GNAO1-related disease (NEDIM) is phenotypically proximate yet mechanistically off-axis for neurotransmitter release and is excluded for current clustering purposes. [f94ad5494a3e9ab8, 28dfc2a4aa28527a]
Variant-model differences: STXBP1 shows loss_of_function, whereas CACNA1A comparators include gain_of_function variants in epilepsy cohorts. [87257c69fcfbcdad, df57b34e24ef5206, 4e69b8ecbf6740e9, c3ec464ea6412040]
Variant-model differences: STXBP1 shows loss_of_function, whereas GRIN1 comparators include gain_of_function variants that increase NMDA receptor-mediated charge transfer. [87257c69fcfbcdad, df57b34e24ef5206, c9e703902a0fb3f5, 0211d2b50f1f9730]
Contradictory genotype–phenotype correlations within STXBP1 are reported: no correlation between seizure and ID severity; no correlation between mutation type and seizure/cognitive outcome; and no recurrent variant–syndrome specificity. [b1f9e5eeafbc81d2, e362983ef11a54b1, ddc8cd6784a496fb]
